physical.mounting-hardware: M6 screws, M6 cage nuts and M6 plastic washers, four of each

configs.description: The finger duct as StarTech.com ships CMDUCT1UX, cover fitted.
configs.name: base

configs.description: The same duct with its removable cover taken off, the two finger walls and their slots open to lay a cable in. The cover comes with the duct, so this is an illustration and not a device type.
configs.name: cover-off

gaps.note: the datasheet, the drawing and the quick-start guide state no cable capacity, no fill and no cable count.
gaps.wanted: a cable capacity table, or a stated fill, for the finger duct

gaps.note: the quick-start guide says each corner has a latch that keeps the cover in place, and the drawing marks a small tab at each end of the cover; no view dimensions a latch, and the format has no latch, so the cover is on or off.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of a cover latch, fitted and released

gaps.note: the drawing's end view shows the cover's edges notched where they meet the walls; no section is dimensioned and no gauge is stated, so the cover is drawn as a plate with two straight lips 1.0 mm thick (estimated).
gaps.wanted: a section through the cover and a finger tip
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - the material, colour, standard (EIA RS310-D) and what is in the box are the datasheet's; the quick-start guide lists four screws, four cage nuts and four washers, the datasheet two M6x15 and four M6x12 screws, four cage nuts and four plastic washers.

capacity.note: no document states a cable capacity: the datasheet, the drawing and the quick-start guide are silent, so none is stated and a gap says so.

chassis.note: drawing - 482.6 x 44.0 x 71.6. The plate is the whole width of the rack, its two ends the ears, so the face is drawn whole with its four slots (L43 stands down above 480 mm). The duct between the ears is 435.00. The datasheet's "Product Length 19.0 in" and "Width 2.8 in" are the 482.6 and the 71.6; its "Height 1.7 in" is the 44.0.

color.note: estimated - "Color: Black". The drawing is line work, so the shades are this library's render of black steel, the cover a little lighter than the duct.

cover.note: datasheet - "a removable top cover that makes it easy to add or remove bundled cables quickly"; the quick-start guide says the cover "can be removed for installation or upgrades" and latches with four latches, one in each corner. It is drawn fitted in `base` and absent in `cover-off`.

ears.note: drawing - `positions` states where the ears bolt, for the Rack Builder. The ears are the flat ends of the plate, and the duct stands out of the other face of it: the drawing's side view puts the plate at one end of the 71.60 and the cover at the other, and the datasheet says "Front Mount (Front Only)". So the plate is the ear plane, nothing stands behind the rail, and `at` is 71.6. This states a placement; no dimension changed.

front.note: drawing - the duct from its open side: the cover over the duct and the plate behind it, the ear slots at the four corners. The cover ships fitted, as the datasheet and the quick-start guide picture it, and is a part that comes off (`cover-off`).

full-depth.note: `full-depth: false` - the whole duct stands in front of the rail, 71.6 mm, so the rear face of its rack unit stays free for another part.

guides.note: drawing - the duct is the channel between the two finger walls, run across the rack, the 435.00 between the ears and 42.0 clear between the walls; its finger gap is the 11.00 the drawing dimensions and its pitch the 27.84 estimated above.

left.note: drawing - the end view: the plate at the rear, the two finger walls standing out of it and the cover's face and lips over their tips. The right is the same, turned round.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S OWN DRAWING. StarTech.com publishes CMDUCT1UX_Diagram.pdf (third angle projection, "DO NOT SCALE", millimetres, uploaded 3/18/2025): a front, a rear, a side view and an isometric, with the dimensions 482.60, 435.00, 71.60, 44.00, 465.00, 31.50, 13.00, 11.00 and "phi 6.50". The datasheet (cmduct1ux_datasheet.pdf) lists the same body as "Product Length 19.0 in [48.3 cm]", "Product Width 2.8 in [71.6 mm]" and "Product Height 1.7 in [44.0 mm]", and the quick-start guide (CMDUCT1UX_QSG.pdf) names the parts. The drawing is the one used where they differ; the reseller figures #1098 quotes (61 x 482 x 47) are neither, and are not used. What the drawing does not dimension - the slot pitch and the pass-through holes - is scaled off it at 2.2 to 2.6 px/mm against its own dimensions, and is estimated.

passes.note: estimated - the three oval holes, 100 by 25 mm, scaled off the drawing's rear view. They lie under the cover, which is a lid, so they are declared where the cover can be taken off. The datasheet states no limit on the cable that fits; the maker's note "Power cables may not fit through the holes" is on CABLMANAGERH's datasheet only, not this one.

rear.note: drawing - the back of the plate, the view with the ear slots 465.00 apart and 31.50 apart and three oval holes between them. The data sheet calls them "pass-through holes at the back"; the quick-start guide's rear view labels them "Pass-through Holes". The holes are not dimensioned: scaled at 2.269 px/mm against the 465.00, three obrounds 100 by 25 mm on a 140 pitch, centred on the plate (estimated).

thickness.note: estimated - no document states a gauge. 1.0 mm is taken for the plate, the walls and the cover; the side view draws them as thin sheet.

top.note: drawing - an elevation, rear at the top of the drawing: the plate, the finger wall with fifteen slots and the cover over the front 21.7 mm. The slots are 11.00 wide, the dimension the drawing gives; their pitch (27.84) is counted and scaled off it at 2.607 px/mm against the 435.00 and is estimated. The drawing shows one wall in plan; the end view shows two, the quick-start guide says the fingers are "available along the length on both sides", and the datasheet "a series of fingers on either side". Both walls are therefore the same, so the bottom is the top again. "Either side" is read as the top and the bottom of the one open face, and not as two faces: the plate has no fingers and the cover is at one end only.
